1 Getting started

📋 What iOS deployment needs, in order

① Certificate
→
② App ID
→
③ Profile
→
④ ASC app
→
⑤ API Key

Go in this order. TestFlight uploads need the app registered in App Store Connect first.

✅ Before you start

  • ⚠️ This is the most common cause of build failures

    flutter create writes the Dart SDK requirement into pubspec.yaml based on your local Flutter version. If CI runs an older Flutter, dependency install fails with version solving failed.

    # 1) Your Flutter/Dart version
    flutter --version
    # 2) Dart version pubspec requires
    grep -A2 '^environment:' pubspec.yaml
    # 3) Version set in CI
    grep -rn 'FLUTTER_VERSION:' .github/workflows/

    If 3 is lower than 1, set the workflow's FLUTTER_VERSION to match your local version. (update the Android workflows too)

📍 "Flutter root" means the folder with pubspec.yaml

It can differ from the Git repo root. Enter the folder that holds both pubspec.yaml and the ios/ folder.

my-repo/ ← ❌ repo root (no pubspec.yaml)
├─ .github/
└─ client/ ← ✅ here! Flutter root
   ├─ pubspec.yaml
   └─ ios/

In the usual layout, with pubspec.yaml right at the repo root, the repo root is the Flutter root.

🔍 How to find the absolute path

For security, the browser can't read a folder's absolute path, so type it in.

🍎 macOS / Linux
cd your-project-folder && pwd
Example output:
/Users/hong/projects/myapp
Separator / · starts with /
🪟 Windows
cd your-project-folder && cd
Example output:
C:\Users\hong\projects\myapp
Separator \ · starts with drive letter:

⚠️ iOS builds and signing only work on macOS. On Windows, use this wizard to generate the config files and register GitHub Secrets; GitHub Actions (macOS runner) does the actual build.

The folder that contains .github/. Fill this in only for a monorepo (Flutter lives in a subfolder such as client/).

2 Create a Distribution certificate Do this first!

🔑 Why the certificate comes first: you need it to create the Provisioning Profile!

Open the Apple Developer Certificates page

🗺️ Overall flow (go in order)

2-0. Check what you have → 2-1. Create a CSR → 2-2. Issue the certificate → 2-3. Export the .p12

If you already have a valid certificate, jump from 2-0 straight to 2-3.

✅ 2-0. Check first: do you already have a certificate?

Run this command in a terminal.

security find-identity -v -p codesigning
If you see "Apple Distribution: ..."
You already have one! Skip 2-1 · 2-2 and go straight to 2-3 (.p12 export) below.
If you only see "Apple Development", or nothing
You have no distribution certificate. Start from 2-1. (A Development certificate can't distribute.)

⚠️ Limit: at most 3 Apple Distribution certificates per account

If you already have 3, you can't create a new one. On the Certificates page, click an expired or unused certificate → Revoke it, then try again.

Before you revoke: Provisioning Profiles signed with that certificate become invalid and must be recreated. However, apps already released on the App Store are not affected.

📝 2-1. Create a CSR (Certificate Signing Request) file

Creating the CSR generates a private key on that Mac. Create it on the same Mac you'll export the .p12 from.

  1. Open the "Keychain Access" app (⌘+Space → "Keychain")
  2. Menu bar: Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Request a Certificate From a Certificate Authority...
  3. Dialog values
    User Email Address: your Apple Developer account email
    Common Name: [Your Name] Distribution (e.g. HONG GILDONG Distribution)
    CA Email Address: leave it empty
    ⚠️ Request is — the default is wrong!
    ❌ Emailed to the CA (default — not this one!)
    ✅ Saved to disk ← switch to this
    ☐ Let me specify key pair information (leave unchecked)
  4. Continue → save to the Downloads folder (recommended) → Save
    Keep the default file name (CertificateSigningRequest). The commands below use it.
→ creates ~/Downloads/CertificateSigningRequest.certSigningRequest
# Check that it was created correctly (optional)
openssl req -in ~/Downloads/CertificateSigningRequest.certSigningRequest -noout -subject -verify

It's fine if you see verify OK and a Subject like CN=..., C=KR.

💡 If the file doesn't show up in the next step's upload dialog → in Finder, press ⌘+Shift+G and paste ~/Downloads/CertificateSigningRequest.certSigningRequest to select it directly.

📋 2-2. Get the certificate from Apple

  1. Click the Open the Certificates page button above
  2. Click the + button
  3. ⚠️ Important! Pick the right type:
    ✅ Apple Distribution - for App Store distribution (pick this!)
    ❌ iOS Distribution - legacy (don't pick)
    ❌ Apple Development - for development (can't distribute)
  4. Choose File → upload the .certSigningRequest from 2-1 → Continue
  5. Click Download → save apple_distribution.cer (keep the default file name)
  6. ⚠️ Downloading isn't enough — you must install it!
    Double-click the downloaded .cer file. (Or run open ~/Downloads/apple_distribution.cer in a terminal.)
    When the "Add Certificates" window opens — choose the keychain
    ✅ login ← keep the default and click "Add"
    ❌ iCloud / System / System Roots (don't pick)
    The private key lives in the login keychain, so the certificate has to go into the same keychain to pair up and export as a .p12.
  7. Check the install: run security find-identity -v -p codesigning in a terminal → success if you see Apple Distribution
If you get a "maximum number of certificates" error → revoke an existing certificate as described in the 2-0 limit note.

📤 2-3. Export the .p12 file from the keychain

  1. Open the "Keychain Access" app on your Mac (⌘+Space → "Keychain")
  2. Left: the "login" keychain → top: the "My Certificates" category (the "Certificates" tab mixes in Apple CAs and gets confusing)
  3. ⚠️ Don't panic if the list shows about 10 certificates
    Most are intermediate CA certificates Apple installed automatically. Leave them alone.
    Developer ID Certification Authority
    Apple Worldwide Developer Relations CA
    Apple Root CA … ❌ ignore all of these
    ▶ Apple Distribution: Name (TEAMID) ← ✅ this one!
    ▶ Apple Development: Name (TEAMID) ← ❌ for development, can't distribute
    How to tell: the name starts with "Apple Distribution:", and there's a ▶ triangle on the left (= it has a private key). CA certificates have no triangle.
  4. ⚠️ First check that the private key is there!
    Expand the ▶ triangle left of the certificate; you should see a 🔑 private key under it.
    Without a private key the .p12 format won't even appear → the certificate was created on another Mac. Get the .p12 from that Mac, or start over from 2-1.
  5. Right-click the certificate → "Export "Apple Distribution: ..."..."
  6. Save dialog
    Save As: apple_distribution.p12
    Where: Downloads
    File Format: Personal Information Exchange (.p12)
    If the format dropdown has no .p12, you picked a certificate without a private key → go back to the step above.
  7. 🔑 Enter the password twice (Password · Verify)
    The password you set here becomes the GitHub Secret APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD. Write it down.
    If you forget it, export the .p12 again (no need to reissue the certificate).
  8. Enter your macOS login password → Allow (Keychain confirming the private key export)
# Check that the private key is really inside (recommended)
openssl pkcs12 -in ~/Downloads/apple_distribution.p12 -nodes -passin pass:YOUR_PASSWORD | grep -c "PRIVATE KEY"

A result of 1 means it's fine. 0 or Mac verify error means the password is wrong or there's no private key.

🔒 The .p12 holds your private key — handle with care

  • Never commit it to Git. If it leaks, anyone can sign apps in your name
  • Back it up with its password somewhere safe (e.g. a password manager)
  • This file alone recovers you on a new Mac — lose it and you must reissue the certificate, using up another of the 3 slots

📍 Where to look in Keychain Access

Default Keychains
login
iCloud
System Keychains
System
System Roots
Category tabs at the top
All Items Passwords Secure Notes My Certificates Keys Certificates

At this point you'll see one of two screens:

A. The list is empty 😰
(no items)
That's normal! Nothing is broken. It just means you haven't been issued a certificate yet.
→ Start from 2-1 (create a CSR) above.
Creating a CSR doesn't change this list. Items appear only after you double-click the .cer in 2-2.
B. A certificate shows up 🎉
▼ 📜
Apple Distribution: Team
Expires: June 8, 2027
🔑 private key ← required!
Expand the ▼ triangle and check that the private key is there.
→ Go to 2-3 (.p12 export).
💡 The "My Certificates" tab shows only certificates that have a private key. If it shows under "Certificates" but not under "My Certificates", there's no private key → you can't export it as a .p12.

🎯 Made it this far? — final check

security find-identity -v -p codesigning

Step 2 is done if you see Apple Distribution like below:

1) 88BE0B2E... "Apple Development: Name (TEAMID)"
2) A278F54B... "Apple Distribution: Name (TEAMID)"
   2 valid identities found
✅ Apple Distribution certificate installed in the keychain
✅ ~/Downloads/apple_distribution.p12 created
✅ .p12 password written down

3 Register the App ID (Bundle ID)

📱 What's an App ID? It's your app's unique identifier. It must match your Flutter Bundle ID!

Open the Apple Developer Identifiers page

📋 How to register the App ID

  1. Click the button above → open the Identifiers page
  2. Click the + button
  3. Step 1: Register a new identifier
    ◉ App IDs ← pick this!
  4. Step 2: Select a type
    ◉ App ← pick this! (not App Clip)
  5. Step 3: Set the Bundle ID
    Description: app name (e.g. My Flutter App)
    ◉ Explicit ← pick this!
    Bundle ID: kr.mycompany.myapp
  6. Step 4: Capabilities — the list has about 150 entries
    You don't need to check most of them. Capabilities only cover features that use Apple server infrastructure or go beyond the sandbox.
    ✅ Check if it applies:
    • Push Notifications — push notifications (needs a separate .p8 key)
    • Sign In with Apple — Apple login
    • In-App Purchase — in-app payments
    • Associated Domains — deep links / universal links
    • HealthKit · iCloud · Maps — if you use those frameworks
    ❌ Don't check these — Info.plist handles them
    Camera · microphone recording · speech recognition (STT) · TTS · location · photo library · Bluetooth
    These ask the user for permission at runtime, so they have nothing to do with provisioning. Just add the NS...UsageDescription strings to Info.plist.
    ⚠️ Siri is for "invoke my app with Siri" (SiriKit). It's unrelated to in-app speech recognition, so don't check it.
    💡 You can add them later, but then you must recreate the Provisioning Profile (repeat step 4). Check features you're sure about now.
  7. Click Register!

📍 Identifiers page preview

Certificates
Identifiers
Devices
Profiles
Identifiers + ← click!
NAME IDENTIFIER
MyApp kr.mycompany.myapp

💡 Bundle ID naming guide

Recommended format: [reverse-domain].[app-name]
✅ kr.mycompany.myapp
✅ com.mycompany.myapp
✅ io.github.username.appname
❌ myapp - too short
❌ MyApp - uppercase not recommended

Must match the Bundle Identifier in your Flutter project's ios/Runner.xcodeproj

⚠️ Compare with your Xcode project before registering

grep PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj

Flutter's default (com.example.appname etc.) is often still there. If it differs from what you register with Apple, signing fails.

If they differ, fix it now. Change the RunnerTests entries too. You can't change the Bundle ID after the App Store release.

Already have it →

4 Create the Provisioning Profile

🔗 What's a Provisioning Profile? A file that bundles the certificate + App ID to prove "this app is signed with this certificate".

⚠️ You need the step 2 certificate + step 3 App ID first!

Open the Apple Developer Profiles page

📋 How to create the Provisioning Profile

  1. Click the button above → open the Profiles page
  2. Click the + button
  3. ⚠️ Pick the Distribution type (not Development!)
    Development
    ○ iOS App Development
    Distribution
    ◉ App Store Connect ← pick this!
    ○ Ad Hoc
  4. Choose the App ID
    the one from step 3 kr.mycompany.myapp select
  5. Choose the Certificate
    the one from step 2 Apple Distribution check the certificate
  6. Enter the profile name
    e.g. MyApp AppStore Distribution
  7. Generate → Download → save the .mobileprovision (unlike the step 2 .p12, no keychain install needed — just keep the file)
  8. ✅ Check that it was created correctly (recommended)
    A profile is a signed binary, not text, so it looks garbled if you just open it. Check its contents with the command below.
    security cms -D -i ~/Downloads/your-file.mobileprovision | plutil -p - | grep -E "Name|application-identifier|ExpirationDate|aps-environment"
    What to check:
    • application-identifier looks like TEAMID.yourBundleID
    • aps-environment is production (if push is on)
    • ExpirationDate is a year from now
    ⚠️ If get-task-allow is true, you made a development profile by mistake → recreate it as Distribution.

💡 Profile naming guide

Recommended format: [app name] [purpose] [type]
✅ MyApp AppStore Distribution
✅ MyApp App Store Dist
✅ ProjectName-AppStore-2024

⚠️ Remember this exact name! You'll enter it into GitHub Secrets.

🚨 It must match exactly, spaces included! One character off and the build fails!

📄
Drag a .mobileprovision file here or click

Exactly the same as the name you entered in Apple Developer!

5 Register the app in App Store Connect Required for TestFlight!

🎯 Why this step is required: the app must be registered in App Store Connect before you can upload to TestFlight!

Fastlane's pilot/upload_to_testflight finds the app by Bundle ID. Without the app you get an "App not found" error!

Open App Store Connect - My Apps

📋 How to register a new app

  1. Click the button above → open App Store Connect
  2. Click the + button → choose New App
  3. New App dialog values
    Platforms:
    ☑ iOS ☐ macOS ☐ tvOS
    Name:
    app display name
    Shown on the App Store (e.g. Ear Location Alert)
    Primary Language: English (or your app's main language)
    Bundle ID:
    kr.mycompany.myapp
    ↑ pick the Bundle ID you registered in step 3 from the dropdown!
    SKU:
    MYAPP2026
    for internal identification (any unique value; must not clash with your other apps)
    User Access:
    ◉ Full Access ○ Limited Access
  4. Click the Create button!

Add a new app!

💡 Pro Tips

  • ✓ You can change the Name later! Edit it anytime in App Store Connect.
  • ⚠️ The Bundle ID can't be changed! Once linked, it stays until you delete the app.
  • ✓ The SKU is internal! Users never see it. It just has to be unique.
  • ✓ Fill in app info later! For now you only need the app "shell". Icons and screenshots come later.

6 Review app info and extra settings

✅ Review what you entered in the earlier steps, then fill in the rest.

📍 How to find your Team ID

Open the Apple Developer Membership page

Find the "Team ID" entry on the page (10 letters and digits)

Or read it straight from the profile you got in step 4:

security cms -D -i ~/Downloads/your-file.mobileprovision | plutil -p - | grep -A2 TeamIdentifier

7 App Store Connect API Key (.p8)

🔑 What's an API Key? The key Fastlane uses to upload to TestFlight automatically.

Open the App Store Connect API Keys page

📋 How to create the API Key

  1. Click the button above → open App Store Connect
  2. On the Team Keys tab, click the + button
  3. Name: something easy to recognize (e.g. MY-PROJECT-KEY)
  4. Access: choose Admin (recommended)
  5. Generate → download the .p8 file right away!
    💡 The Key ID is in the file name
    AuthKey_9S3Y25UVZN.p8 → Key ID = 9S3Y25UVZN
    Even if you didn't write it down, the file name tells you.
  6. If you already have a .p8
    Reuse it instead of creating a new one. But check that its Key ID is still in the Active Keys list in App Store Connect.
    Revoked keys disappear from the list, and uploads fail even if you have the file.
    # Check the file format (EC P-256 means it's fine)
    openssl pkcs8 -in ~/Downloads/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 -nocrypt | openssl ec -noout -text | grep NIST

📍 Where to find it on the App Store Connect page

Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API
⬇️ shown separately in the middle of the page
Issuer ID ⓘ
xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx Copy
↑ click the Copy button here!
Active Keys ●
NAME GENERATED BY KEY ID ACCESS
MY-PROJECT-KEY Jane Doe XXXXXXXXXX Admin
↑ copy the Key ID from the table!

💡 Pro Tips

  • ✓ One Admin key manages every project! You can use the same API Key for multiple apps.
  • ✓ The Issuer ID is shared by the whole team! Every API Key uses the same Issuer ID.
  • ⚠️ The .p8 file can be downloaded only once! Back it up right after creating it.

8 Generate the Fastlane files

🚀 What's Fastlane? A tool that automates iOS builds & deployment. GitHub Actions uses it.

New files:

  • ios/Gemfile — Fastlane dependencies
  • ios/fastlane/Fastfile — TestFlight upload lane
  • ios/ExportOptions.plist — IPA export settings

Existing files that change:

  • ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj — Bundle ID, Manual Signing, Team ID
  • ios/Runner/Info.plist — encryption setting (ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption)
  • ios/.gitignore — adds Gemfile.lock

⚠️ If the Bundle ID differs from what you entered in step 3, it's changed automatically. No Appfile is created — app identifiers are injected as GitHub Actions environment variables, so it isn't needed.

⚠️ The project path is empty

Go back to step 1 and enter the Flutter project's absolute path. Running it as is fails with cd: no such file or directory.

📌 Why there are two paths

cd goes to the repo root where the script lives, and the argument points to the Flutter root with pubspec.yaml. In a monorepo the two differ, so they have to be split like this. 

cd "/path/to/project" && python3 ".github/util/flutter/testflight-wizard/testflight-wizard.py" setup ...

✓ Done! GitHub Secrets values

🎉 All set! Register the values below as GitHub Secrets.

📍 How to register GitHub Secrets

  1. GitHub repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
  2. Click "New repository secret"
  3. Enter the Name and Value of each item below
  4. When you're done, delete the downloaded github-secrets files

Secrets to register

📦 Export / import settings

🗑️ Once the secrets are registered, delete the downloaded github-secrets files. They contain your certificate and keys as is.

If JSON/TXT/ZIP exports stay in your Downloads folder, anyone can pull out your distribution certificate and App Store Connect key.

Restore your settings from a JSON file you exported earlier.

📝 What each secret is

APPLE_CERTIFICATE_BASE64

The distribution certificate (.p12), Base64-encoded

APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD

The password you set when exporting the .p12

APPLE_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64

The provisioning profile (.mobileprovision), Base64-encoded

APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_BASE64

The App Store Connect API Key (.p8), Base64-encoded

APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_ID

API Key ID (10 characters)

APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID

App Store Connect Issuer ID (UUID format)

IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_NAME

The profile name from step 4 (e.g. MyApp AppStore Distribution)

IOS_BUNDLE_ID

The Bundle ID registered in step 3 (e.g. kr.mycompany.myapp)

APPLE_TEAM_ID

Apple Team ID (10 letters and digits)

➕ Extra secrets (optional) (open the separate tool →)

Add anything else you need, such as extra provisioning profiles or env files.
Text files like 📄 .json/.yml/.env are kept as is, binary files like 🔐 .p12/.mobileprovision/.p8 are converted to Base64 automatically.

🎛️ Deploy mode & release roadmap (iOS)

The GitHub repo Variables → IOS_DEPLOY_MODE sets the default deploy scope. A deploy_mode input on a manual workflow run takes precedence.

  • store_only — up to the TestFlight upload (default)
  • store_prepare — up to just before App Store submission (a person clicks 'Add for Review' in ASC)
  • store_submit — submits for App Store review automatically

⚠️ A new app needs one manual submission in App Store Connect first; updates after that are automated with store_submit.

'What's New' text — defaults to that version's CHANGELOG entry. If you'd rather not show reviewers the details, put a one-line text in STORE_WHATS_NEW_OVERRIDE under the workflow file's env. TestFlight 'What to Test' is not affected.

Per-language notes — if the store has several languages, list them in metadata.template.options.store_locales in version.yml (e.g. ["ko-KR", "en-US", "ja-JP", "zh-CN"]; the first is the default language). /pro-changelog-deploy drafts the translations for approval when it writes the release notes, and languages without a translation get the default-language text (the store rejects empty fields). Without the key, a single text is uploaded as today.

If only the App Store has a different language set, list just this store in store_locales_ios (e.g. ["ko-KR", "en-US"]). Language codes the App Store doesn't have are skipped, not uploaded.

⚠️ If the list has a language the App Store doesn't have, deliver enables that language for the app. If your App Store languages differ, narrow it with store_locales_ios.

Review notes — if ios/fastlane/review_notes.txt exists its contents are sent every time; otherwise the existing App Store Connect value is kept.
